solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sails in container vessel

parts.note: a can is a tin container
vas is the anatomical term for a duct or vessel, as in vas deferens

explanation.surface: Sails being carried aboard a container ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails were traditionally made of heavy cotton cloth, so the fabric names the sails themselves.

clue.text: A female horse soldier can be unyielding

parts.note: a dam is the mother of a horse
a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A mare and a cavalryman both refuse to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone firmly refusing to change their mind is described this way.

clue.text: Watch self-appointed policeman stake out

indicators.note: out tells us the stake is removed from the policeman word

parts.note: a vigilante takes the law into their own hands
an ante is the stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A self-styled lawman watches over a stakeout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake out' looks like the police phrase, but it splits: the stake is taken out of the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: keeping watch through the night is keeping a vigil.

clue.text: Drowsy drunken man, in the end, lost most of money

indicators.note: drunken signals the gathered letters are jumbled about
in the end picks only the final letter of the word man

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of means the word money loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A sleepy drunk who has ended up losing nearly all his cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' looks like it describes the man, but it is the anagram signal for N, LOST and MONE (money short of its Y).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sleepy, heavy-eyed person is described with this Latin-derived word.

clue.text: Leader in Long Island to fix what's crucial to plan

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of Long

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: A chief on Long Island arranging the key part of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long Island' looks like one place, but only Long gives its first letter; Island alone is INCH, a Scottish term for an islet.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the vital element holding a scheme together is called this, after the pin that keeps a wheel on its axle.

clue.text: Included vitamin in revamped 11 medicine

indicators.note: included says one piece is placed inside the other
revamped says the letters of the referenced entry are reworked

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning slight
C is vitamin C

explanation.surface: A remedy reformulated with an added vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of the 11 answer (from 'revamped') and put C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a syrupy cough remedy is a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Canteen's vulgar as reported by Independent

indicators.note: as reported means we go by how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: naff is British slang for tacky or vulgar

explanation.surface: A newspaper report calls a canteen tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs canteens for British servicemen; NAFF is British slang for tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the service organisation's name is used for the military canteen or shop it runs.

clue.text: Uncomfortable reminder of past misdeeds in Barnet ruined his party with no compensation

parts.note: Barnet (Barnet Fair) is Cockney rhyming slang for hair

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of his party are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: pay is compensation for work

explanation.surface: Someone in Barnet whose party fell apart and who got nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London district, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair. HIS PARTY without the letters of PAY leaves HISRT, rearranged to SHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: penitents wore a scratchy goat-hair garment, so the phrase now means a self-imposed penance or reminder of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Frozen sheet could make one feel cold around centre of abdomen

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the central letter

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters may be formed into something new
centre of picks the middle letter of abdomen

explanation.surface: Something that might give you a chill in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges I, FEEL and C to ICEFLE, which goes 'around' O, the middle of abdomen.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a flat mass of floating sea ice is a frozen sheet.

clue.text: Dithering in vague matter becomes contentious

indicators.note: dithering means wavering about, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: Wavering over something vague leads to a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone always ready to quarrel or dispute is called contentious.

clue.text: So fit all torn 1 here

indicators.note: torn says the words are ripped apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Torn sails get fixed here, so everything fits.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' refers to the answer at 1 across, sails; this is where they are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sailmaker's workshop, usually an upper floor, is where sails are cut and sewn.

clue.text: Slight changes in sunlit characters

indicators.note: changes in says the letters of sunlit are changed in order

explanation.surface: Small shifts in sunlit figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a noun, a slight is a snub or affront.

clue.text: Prevent swelling round top of muscle with a touch of ice

indicators.note: round says the swelling goes around the other letters

parts.note: a stye is a swelling on the eyelid

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter
a touch of gives just the first letter of ice

explanation.surface: Stopping a swollen muscle by applying a little ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obstruct or thwart someone's progress, originally a golf term.

clue.text: Attraction of male foreign agent is masculine

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange, so the letters of agent are rearranged

parts.note: M is also the abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: The allure of a man who is a spy from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: personal allure or the physical pull between poles is magnetism.

clue.text: Filter water in Southern territory

indicators.note: in places the water inside the other letters

parts.note: TER is an abbreviation for territory
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Filtering the water supply somewhere in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sieve or colander used to separate solids from liquid.

clue.text: Salad ingredient set around final four portions of gnocchi

indicators.note: around says the radio goes on both sides of the gnocchi letters

parts.note: a radio set, so set means radio

indicators.note: final four portions of takes the last four letters of gnocchi

explanation.surface: A dish arranged around the last few pieces of gnocchi.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bitter red-leaved chicory used in Italian salads.

clue.text: Scamp hides in British boat

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A young rascal stows away on a British boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: British informal word for a rascal or annoying person.

clue.text: Inspection of toilet search's back to front

parts.note: loo is British informal for toilet

indicators.note: back to front moves the last letter of the search word to its start

parts.note: to seek is to search

explanation.surface: Searching a toilet thoroughly from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a quick look or check.

clue.text: Strangely in dreams loss of article jogs memory

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are rearranged oddly

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Odd dreams in which things are lost bring memories back.
explanation.walkthrough: IN DREAMS minus the A ('loss of article') leaves letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that prompts recollection is said to remind you, a verb phrase matching the third person.

clue.text: Take away section of home-made tachometer

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Removing part of a homemade rev counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to separate or remove one thing from another.

clue.text: Dog starts to devour evening's rabbit stew

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A dog begins wolfing down the rabbit stew served in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thick seafood or vegetable soup-stew.

clue.text: Concealed panic finally evident

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of panic

parts.note: overt means open and evident

explanation.surface: Hidden alarm eventually becomes plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident' and the answer are near opposites, a neat contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: secret or hidden, as in a clandestine operation.

clue.text: Symbol for county? Not quite

parts.note: to can mean for, as in a toast to someone

indicators.note: not quite says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Kent is an English county

explanation.surface: Asking what emblem represents a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a token is a sign or emblem standing for something.

clue.text: Military intelligence ordered doctor to reveal miniaturised picture

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of doctor are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Army spies order a doctor to disclose a hidden image.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a photograph reduced to the size of a dot, used in espionage.

clue.text: Sea-ear's first of two with no top

indicators.note: with no top removes the first letter in this down clue

parts.note: the former is the first of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A shell named first of a topless pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the abalone, an ear-shaped shellfish, is also known as the sea-ear.

clue.text: Spooner's Irishman in the horse farm is an old fogey

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: Mick is a stereotypical name for an Irishman
a stud is a farm for breeding horses

explanation.surface: An Irishman on a stud farm turns out to be terribly old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person who resists change and is stuck in their ways.

clue.text: Name in States for a boundary stone

parts.note: a term is a name for something
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Naming a border marker in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sense: Terminus was the Roman god of boundaries, and the word names a boundary marker.

clue.text: Lorry, not large, carrying Queen's clockwork model

indicators.note: carrying says the remaining letters hold the queen inside
not means the letter for large is left out

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A truck transporting the monarch's mechanical toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a mechanical model of the solar system, often clockwork-driven.
